commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: Move user message construction from Neil
commitResults.messageBody:
Neil constructs user-facing messages, mixing application coordination
with presentation concerns.

Move task-related message formatting into Ui so Neil focuses on
coordinating application logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Gradle: Set Neil as application main class
Test: Add coverage for core task logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Task parsing, list management, and storage are core workflows with
limited automated coverage. Regressions in these paths can reach users
without early feedback.

Add JUnit tests for task state and decoding, parser validation, list
operations, and persistence. Document a target of testing the
highest-value 50% of methods and updating tests alongside code changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add keyword search for task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need a quick way to locate tasks without scanning the entire list.

Add a find command that searches task descriptions case-insensitively,
preserves result order, and rejects commands without a search term.

Add tests for parsing, matching, result ordering, and UI output.

The project relies on manual review to enforce Java coding style.

Style violations can therefore be missed or applied inconsistently.

Let's add the SE-EDU Checkstyle rules to Gradle and verify production
and test code as part of the standard check lifecycle.

Update existing test formatting so the codebase passes the new checks.

Neil accepts commands only through terminal input, which limits the
application to a CLI workflow.

Add an FXML-based chatbot window that displays user commands and Neil's
responses as dialog bubbles. Route commands through the existing parser,
task list, and storage logic so behavior and persistence remain unchanged.

Configure Gradle with JavaFX and make the GUI the application entry point.
Close the application when the user enters `bye`, matching the CLI exit
behavior. Add tests for command responses and persistence.

Document assumptions about task-list contents, parser command
coverage, FXML injection and controller initialization.

These assertions expose programming and validation errors close
to their source while preserving validation for user-controlled input.

Separate task status and subtype decoding into focused helpers so that
the main decoding workflow is easier to read and maintain.

Add coverage for rejecting deadline and event records with extra fields.
Add assertions for internal invariants

Separate deadline and event parsing into focused helpers so that the
main task parsing workflow is easier to read and extend.

Strengthen tests for commands containing extra whitespace.

commitResults.messageTitle: Help command: Add in-app command guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Users have no way to discover supported commands from within the app.

Add a help command that displays grouped command descriptions and
examples. Mention it in the welcome message and user guide, and keep it
available when task storage cannot be loaded.

Fixed message widths waste horizontal space when the window grows and large avatars make user commands visually equal to app responses.

Use proportional message widths, remove the user avatar, and reduce Neil's badge so long replies remain readable while the conversation keeps a clear visual hierarchy.

Error responses look identical to ordinary Neil messages, making
invalid commands easy to overlook.

Return typed command results and render errors with a clear heading,
red accent border, and higher-contrast colors. This avoids coupling
visual behavior to specific message wording.

The input controls blend into the chat area and allow blank commands to
be submitted, which weakens visual hierarchy and interaction feedback.

Group the controls in a responsive composer bar, prevent blank
submissions, and style the button's hover, pressed, focused, and
disabled states.

commitResults.messageTitle: GUI: Show help in a scrollable table
commitResults.messageBody:
The plain-text help list is difficult to scan and wraps poorly in
narrow windows.

Present commands, purposes, and examples in aligned columns with
horizontal scrolling when space is limited. Tag help responses
explicitly so only help content receives the specialized layout.

Events accepted arbitrary time text, allowing invalid dates and end times
that were not later than their start times.

Parse event boundaries using strict date-time values and reject malformed,
equal, or reversed ranges. Apply the same validation when loading saved
tasks and document the required input format.

The exit check required bye to match the entire raw input, so harmless surrounding whitespace caused the command to be rejected.

Strip surrounding whitespace before the case-insensitive comparison. Keep rejecting input that includes additional arguments.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Preserve tasks during failed saves
commitResults.messageBody:
Direct writes could leave the task file partially written when a save
was interrupted or the disk ran out of space.

Write and flush a complete temporary file before replacing saved data.
Use atomic replacement when supported so the previous data remains
available if saving fails.

Unmarking, deleting, invalid task numbers, and commands following a
startup storage failure lacked end-to-end coverage.

Add workflow tests that verify responses, in-memory task state, and
saved file contents remain consistent across these paths.

Storage tests did not cover directory targets, malformed UTF-8 input,
or clearing all saved tasks.

Add cases that verify invalid storage inputs produce domain errors and
that saving an empty task list creates a valid empty file.
